prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The area-balance tolerance of the partitioner (area_balance_error=0.1) is quite tight, forcing the partitioner to move non-critical macros to satisfy balance; loosening it to 0.15 lets the cut objective keep timing-relevant macros on their preferred tier, reducing cross-tier detours and TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=-0.077 robust(mean-std)=-0.077 min_case=-0.095 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=-0.009 dWNS=+5.0% dTNS=-4.4% overflow~116
  bp-ng45: score=+0.027 dWNS=-4.1% dTNS=+7.2% overflow~149
  bp_fe-ng45: score=-0.095 dWNS=-14.1% dTNS=-6.5% overflow~150
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis not supported: total score −0.077, all cases valid, but only bp-ng45 improved (+0.027, dTNS +7.2%). ariane133-ng45 was slightly negative (−0.009) despite dWNS +5.0% and dTNS −4.4%, and bp_fe-ng45 regressed sharply (−0.095, dWNS −14.1%), suggesting looser balance let timing-critical macros drift to worse tiers there. Mechanism is case-dependent, not general. Next step: sweep area_balance_error (0.10–0.15) per design, or apply 0.15 only where tier capacity is asymmetric, and re-check bp_fe-ng45 macro-tier assignments.
